findings.finding: The 7 treads are evenly spaced, equal-height light bars with thin dark gaps. The upper steps are not visibly thinner or darker, so at 1x the flight reads partly as a ladder or rack rather than a rising stair.
findings.fix: Shrink the tread/riser pitch toward the top (e.g. 3/3/2/2/2/1/1 px risers) and step the tread colour down one palette shade on each of the top three steps.

findings.finding: Dark bands of equal weight run down BOTH sides of the flight, so the stair looks set into a trench. The intended east-only wedge shadow does not stand out from the west side.
findings.fix: Replace the west dark band with the stone-handrail highlight colour. On the east keep a 1-2px shadow that widens toward the south (a wedge), using the floor-shadow colour instead of the outline colour.

findings.finding: The landing's dark front face is barely distinguishable from the flanking dark bands, so the raised landing reads weakly.
findings.fix: Give the landing top a 1px light top edge, and draw its front face as a distinct 2px mid-dark stone strip with mortar ticks, separate from the side shadow.

findings.finding: The interior treads are uniform stripes. The darkening toward the north is gradual but the far end is not clearly near-black at 1x.
findings.fix: Make the top two tread rows the darkest palette navy/black. Drop the tread highlight pixels on the north half so the depth falloff reads at 1x.

findings.finding: The 'hatch opening' at the top is a dark horizontal rectangle with a flat iron rim lying in the floor plane. No vertical element rises above it, so in the shipped gear room it reads as a hole or trapdoor in the floor at the top of the flight. The piece reads as a stair leading down into a pit, or a ramp onto a trapdoor, not as an UP stair into a hatch.
findings.fix: Turn the top row into an upright frame. Draw two 2px riveted iron posts rising from the landing corners with a lintel bar across the top row. Fill only the area inside the posts with dark, and show a lit iron landing plate (with rivets and a highlight) in front of the opening. Add a cast shadow on the floor east of the posts so the frame reads as standing up.

findings.finding: The flight is boxed by dark navy side bands on both sides plus a dark base. At 1x the piece looks like a crate or ladder lying on the floor rather than a rising stair.
findings.fix: Lighten the handrails to the iron mid-tone with brass caps on the newels. Remove the dark west band and keep only an east-side wedge shadow.

findings.finding: The warm-lit top steps are good, but the lower cellar treads are uniform brown bars at equal spacing, so the rise is shown only by the light change, not by geometry.
findings.fix: Shorten the riser height on the upper four steps and add a 1px dark riser line under each lit tread so the steps step back into the doorway.

findings.finding: The 'door frame' at the top is a dark filled rectangle under a plank lintel, with no visible posts standing up from the landing. Combined with dark side bands, it reads like the owl-down stairwell hole. At 1x, owl-up and owl-down share the same wooden framing and dark top, so a player cannot tell up from down at a glance.
findings.fix: Draw 2px wooden door posts in the top row, rising above the lintel line, with a lit 1px edge on the west post. Make the doorway interior dark only between the posts, with a lit plank landing (straw specks) in front. Lighten the treads so the stair is clearly brighter toward the door, the opposite of the down stairwell's darkening.

findings.finding: Straw and droppings specks are sparse and barely visible; the rough-stone treads read as plain grey stripes.
findings.fix: Add 2-3 straw-yellow and 2 white dropping pixels per tread row, plus irregular 1px chips along tread edges.

findings.finding: The north rail balusters are fine, but the side rails are thin. The south lip is a narrow light strip that barely separates from the floor.
findings.fix: Widen the south lip to a 2px light plank edge with a 1px dark front, and thicken the west/east rail posts to 2px at the corners.

places.finding: Clocktower gear room: the clock-stair's top hatch sits in open floor mid-room, with no wall behind it. As drawn it reads as a pit or trapdoor at the north end of a short ramp, not a way up to the upper gallery (same root cause as the piece-level major).
places.fix: Use the upright posts-and-lintel hatch fix above, and/or move the stair so its top row abuts the north wall face. Alternatively add a short iron gallery beam above the hatch spanning to the wall.

places.finding: Owlery: the down stairwell's west rail sits flush against the west wall trim with no floor gap, so it reads as slightly jammed into the wall.
places.fix: Shift the stairwell one tile east, or draw a 1px floor/shadow column between the rail and the wall trim.

places.finding: Honeydukes: the stair frame sits correctly in the wall face between the bookshelves. However, the bottom step row meets the cellar floor with no shadow or base line, so it looks pasted on.
places.fix: Add a 1px dark floor-contact line under the bottom tread and small newel-post shadows on the floor.
